narrative_before: Attackers (believed to be acting for the Chinese government) used a phishing email to gain access to the Starwood brands' reservation system (Senate testimony). They obtained valid passwords and accounts, including an administrator account, using tools such as Mimikatz and planted a remote access trojan to move laterally within the network. Using the admin account they queried the network for databases with relevant customer information, discovered them, and compressed and encrypted the data before exfiltrating it, deleting the staged files afterward. The breach, undetected from 2014 until 2018, exposed personal information (including passport numbers) of up to ~383 million guests.
